bug_semantics: Portainer CE's Docker proxy transport (api/http/proxy/factory/docker/transport.go) derives the path on which ALL per-operation authorization decisions are made by stripping an API version prefix with an UNANCHORED, UNVALIDATED regex: `var apiVersionRe = regexp.MustCompile(`(/v[0-9]\.[0-9]*)?`)` and `unversionedPath := apiVersionRe.ReplaceAllString(request.URL.Path, "")`. Because the pattern is optional and unanchored it strips any `/vN.M` substring anywhere in the path, and because the raw request path is never normalized (no path.Clean) and no encoded separators are rejected, an authenticated low-privileged user can craft a non-canonical URL (encoded `%2f`/`%5c` separators, embedded version substrings, dot segments) such that the authorization layer (prefixProxyFuncMap routing, isAdminOnlyRoute admin-only checks, restrictedResourceOperation resource-ID extraction) evaluates a DIFFERENT path/resource than the one the Docker daemon or agent ultimately executes — bypassing the Docker proxy authorization middleware entirely and reaching the Docker Engine API with root-equivalent privileges on the host (CWE-287). The fix commit's own comment names the mechanism: 'A percent-encoded path separator lets a request dodge the operation authorization.'
flaw_origin: Commit 19d4db13be80864883745b922def806248f06651 ("feat(api): rewrite access control management in Docker (#3337)", 2019-11-13, author Anthony Lapenna <anthony.lapenna@portainer.io>, committer GitHub) first wrote the vulnerable design in one commit: it introduced BOTH (a) `apiVersionRe = regexp.MustCompile(`(/v[0-9]\.[0-9]*)?`)` — the unanchored version-strip normalizer — and (b) the transport-level per-operation authorization layer that consumes its output (prefix-dispatch proxyFuncMap, administratorOperation/admin-only routes, restrictedResourceOperation keyed on path-extracted resource IDs). Before this commit the Docker proxy had NO path-derived operation authorization (only path-independent endpoint-level AuthorizedEndpointOperation in proxy_docker.go), so no normalization divergence was possible. `git log -S apiVersionRe` on the file shows 19d4db13 as the sole introducer; the vulnerable line survived verbatim (modulo refactors) through 2.44.0. The advisory's named sink — proxy authorization applied to a non-normalized, attacker-malleable path — is born here.

Vulnerability first: the advisory names a proxy-authorization bypass via non-canonical URL normalization in Portainer CE through 2.44.0. Code archaeology: at 2.44.0 the Docker proxy transport authorizes every operation against a path produced by an unanchored optional regex strip, with no path.Clean and no encoded-separator rejection — exactly the 'fails to normalize request paths before applying access controls' defect. The BIC must be the commit that first wrote those vulnerable lines: 19d4db13be80 (2019, #3337) simultaneously introduced the faulty normalizer (apiVersionRe) and the operation-authorization layer that consumes it; `git log -S` confirms it as the regex's sole introducer, and the pre-19d4 proxy had no path-derived authorization at all. Single-commit flaw (squash_decomposed=false). Fix: BE-13269 lands on develop (3df3a2d4) and is backported to release/2.39 (9e5bf2e1), neither in a clone tag, matching the advisory floor 'through 2.44.0'; BIC ancestry (first tag 1.23.0) covers the whole disclosed vulnerable range. AI decision: BIC-only attribution — the BIC object carries only the human identity Anthony Lapenna with no AI marker, so NOT_AI; fix commits likewise human (Devon Steenberg).
